{{short description|Algebraic number fields are determined by their absolute Galois groups}}
In [[mathematics]], the '''Neukirch–Uchida theorem''' shows that all problems about [[algebraic number field]]s can be reduced to problems about their [[absolute Galois group]]s. [[Jürgen Neukirch]] showed that two algebraic number fields with the same absolute Galois group are [[isomorphic]],{{sfnp|Neukirch|1969}}{{sfnp|Neukirch|1969b}} and Kôji Uchida strengthened this by proving Neukirch's conjecture that automorphisms of the algebraic number field correspond to [[outer automorphism]]s of its absolute Galois group.{{sfnp|Uchida|1976}} [[Florian Pop]] extended the result to infinite fields that are [[Finitely generated algebra|finitely generated]] over [[prime field]]s.{{sfnp|Pop|1990}}{{sfnp|Pop|1994}}

The Neukirch–Uchida theorem is one of the foundational results of [[anabelian geometry]], whose main theme is to reduce properties of geometric objects to properties of their [[fundamental group]]s, provided these fundamental groups are sufficiently non-abelian.

==Statement==
Let <math>K_1</math>, <math>K_2</math> be two [[algebraic number field]]s. The '''Neukirch–Uchida theorem''' says that, for every topological group [[isomorphism]]
:<math>\phi:\operatorname{Gal}(\bar K_1/K_1)\to\operatorname{Gal}(\bar K_2/K_2)</math>
of [[absolute Galois group]]s, there exists a unique field isomorphism <math>\sigma:\bar K_1\to\bar K_2</math> such that
:<math>\sigma(K_1)=K_2</math>
and
:<math>\phi(g)=\sigma\circ g\circ\sigma^{-1}</math>
for every <math>g\in\operatorname{Gal}(\bar K_1/K_1)</math>. The following diagram illustrates this condition.
:<math>\begin{matrix}
K_1 & \hookrightarrow & \bar{K_1} & \xrightarrow[\cong]g & \bar{K_1} \\
{\scriptstyle\sigma|_{K_1}}\downarrow & & \downarrow{\scriptstyle\sigma} & & \downarrow{\scriptstyle\sigma} \\
K_2 & \hookrightarrow & \bar{K_2} & \xrightarrow[\phi(g)]{\cong} & \bar{K_2}
\end{matrix}
</math>
In particular, for [[algebraic number field]]s <math>K_1</math>, <math>K_2</math>, the following two conditions are equivalent.
* <math>\operatorname{Gal}(\bar{K_1}/K_1)\cong\operatorname{Gal}(\bar{K_2}/K_2)</math>
* <math>K_1\cong K_2</math>
